tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. I wrote [explore.py](explore.py) and ran it. It reads all four CSVs as plain text and only prints a report, with no changes to the data and no files written. Run it with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python explore.py
```

pandas wasn't installed, so I created a `.venv` and installed it there. `explore.py` isn't committed yet.

What the report shows:

- **Row counts:** patients 300, visits 815, prescriptions 540, lab_results 425.
- **Missing values:** `next_appointment` is empty in 582 visits, `phone` in 8 patients, lab `unit` in 12 rows and lab `reference_range` in 8. No cells contain "NA"-style text or stray spaces.
- **Date formats:** five of the six date columns all use `YYYY-MM-DD`. Lab `collected_on` mixes three shapes: `NN/NN/NNNN` (390 rows), `14 Oct 23` (26) and `2 Oct 23` (9). The slash dates are probably day/month (for example `17/04/2024`), but rows where both numbers are 12 or under can't be told apart for sure. That needs a decision from you, not from me.
- **Test name / unit:** there are 28 combinations. The same tests appear under different names and units:
  - HbA1c as `HbA1c`/`A1C` in %, and as `Glycated Hb` in mmol/mol.
  - Fasting glucose as `FBS`/`Glucose (F)` in mg/dL, and as `Fasting Glucose` in mmol/L.
  - After-meal glucose as `PPBS`/`Glucose (PP)` in mg/dL, and as `Post Prandial Glucose` in mmol/L.

  Several tests also have rows with no unit.
- **Drug names:** 104 distinct spellings. The same drug often appears with prefixes like `T.`, `Tab.`, `TAB` (all caps), `Inj.` or `Syp`, for example `Metformin` / `T. Metformin` / `Tab. Metformin`.
- **Shared phone:** 7 numbers are shared. Four pairs look like the same person registered twice, with the same date of birth and a name variant:
  - Md. Rafiq / Mohammed Rafiq
  - Padmavathi / Padma Reddy
  - Shivakumar / Shivakumar H M
  - Joseph Dsouza / D'Souza

  The other three look like family members sharing one phone, such as the Mulla family.
- **Shared date of birth:** 5 dates are shared, overlapping the duplicates above.

The full output is about 355 lines, including unique-value counts for every column.

"""Clean the raw export into output/clean/. Never writes to export/.

Every change or flag is logged to output/data_issues.csv.

Usage: python clean.py [export_dir] [output_dir]
"""
import re
import shutil
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

EXPORT_DIR = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "export")
OUTPUT_DIR = Path(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "output")
CLEAN_DIR = OUTPUT_DIR / "clean"
UNCHANGED_FILES = ["patients.csv", "visits.csv", "prescriptions.csv"]

# Raw test name -> canonical test name.
TEST_NAMES = {
    "HbA1c": "HbA1c",
    "A1C": "HbA1c",
    "Glycated Hb": "HbA1c",
    "FBS": "Fasting Glucose",
    "Glucose (F)": "Fasting Glucose",
    "Fasting Glucose": "Fasting Glucose",
    "PPBS": "Post Prandial Glucose",
    "Glucose (PP)": "Post Prandial Glucose",
    "Post Prandial Glucose": "Post Prandial Glucose",
}

# (canonical test, raw unit) -> (target unit, conversion, decimals).
# HbA1c: IFCC mmol/mol -> NGSP %, master equation % = 0.09148 * mmol/mol + 2.152.
# Glucose: mmol/L -> mg/dL, x 18.016 (molar mass of glucose / 10).
CONVERSIONS = {
    ("HbA1c", "mmol/mol"): ("%", lambda x: 0.09148 * x + 2.152, 1),
    ("Fasting Glucose", "mmol/L"): ("mg/dL", lambda x: x * 18.016, 0),
    ("Post Prandial Glucose", "mmol/L"): ("mg/dL", lambda x: x * 18.016, 0),
}
TARGET_UNITS = {"HbA1c": "%", "Fasting Glucose": "mg/dL",
                "Post Prandial Glucose": "mg/dL"}

DMY_SLASH = re.compile(r"\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}")
D_MON_YY = re.compile(r"\d{1,2} [A-Z][a-z]{2} \d{2}")

issues = []


def log(file, row_index, mrn, column, old, new, action, reason):
    issues.append({
        "file": file,
        "line": row_index + 2,  # 1-based, after the header line
        "mrn": mrn,
        "column": column,
        "old_value": old,
        "new_value": new,
        "action": action,
        "reason": reason,
    })


def parse_lab_date(raw):
    """Return YYYY-MM-DD. Only DD/MM/YYYY and 'D Mon YY' are accepted."""
    if DMY_SLASH.fullmatch(raw):
        return datetime.strptime(raw, "%d/%m/%Y").strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    if D_MON_YY.fullmatch(raw):
        return datetime.strptime(raw, "%d %b %y").strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    raise ValueError(f"Unrecognised lab date format: {raw!r}")


def fmt(number, decimals):
    return f"{round(number, decimals):.{decimals}f}"


def convert_range(raw, convert, decimals):
    """Convert 'a-b' or '<a' reference ranges; fail loudly on anything else."""
    if m := re.fullmatch(r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)-(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", raw):
        low, high = (convert(float(v)) for v in m.groups())
        return f"{fmt(low, decimals)}-{fmt(high, decimals)}"
    if m := re.fullmatch(r"<(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", raw):
        return f"<{fmt(convert(float(m.group(1))), decimals)}"
    raise ValueError(f"Unrecognised reference range: {raw!r}")


def clean_labs(labs):
    name = "lab_results.csv"
    for col in ["test_name", "value", "unit", "reference_range", "collected_on"]:
        labs[f"raw_{col}"] = labs[col]
    labs["flag"] = ""

    for i, row in labs.iterrows():
        mrn = row["mrn"]

        try:
            parsed = parse_lab_date(row["collected_on"])
        except ValueError as e:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name} line {i + 2} (mrn {mrn}): {e}")
        labs.at[i, "collected_on"] = parsed
        log(name, i, mrn, "collected_on", row["collected_on"], parsed,
            "reformatted", "lab date normalised to YYYY-MM-DD")

        test = TEST_NAMES.get(row["test_name"], row["test_name"])
        if test != row["test_name"]:
            labs.at[i, "test_name"] = test
            log(name, i, mrn, "test_name", row["test_name"], test,
                "renamed", "test name mapped to canonical name")

        unit = row["unit"]
        if unit == "":
            labs.at[i, "flag"] = "missing_unit"
            log(name, i, mrn, "unit", "", "", "flagged",
                "unit missing; value not converted, unit not guessed")
            continue

        if (test, unit) in CONVERSIONS:
            target_unit, convert, decimals = CONVERSIONS[(test, unit)]
            new_value = fmt(convert(float(row["value"])), decimals)
            labs.at[i, "value"] = new_value
            labs.at[i, "unit"] = target_unit
            log(name, i, mrn, "value", row["value"], new_value, "converted",
                f"{unit} -> {target_unit}")
            log(name, i, mrn, "unit", unit, target_unit, "converted",
                f"{unit} -> {target_unit}")
            if row["reference_range"]:
                new_range = convert_range(row["reference_range"], convert, decimals)
                labs.at[i, "reference_range"] = new_range
                log(name, i, mrn, "reference_range", row["reference_range"],
                    new_range, "converted", f"{unit} -> {target_unit}")
        elif test in TARGET_UNITS and unit != TARGET_UNITS[test]:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name} line {i + 2} (mrn {mrn}): no conversion "
                             f"defined for {test} in {unit!r}")
    return labs


def main():
    CLEAN_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    labs = pd.read_csv(EXPORT_DIR / "lab_results.csv", dtype=str,
                       keep_default_na=False)
    clean_labs(labs).to_csv(CLEAN_DIR / "lab_results.csv", index=False)

    for name in UNCHANGED_FILES:
        shutil.copyfile(EXPORT_DIR / name, CLEAN_DIR / name)

    pd.DataFrame(issues, columns=["file", "line", "mrn", "column", "old_value",
                                  "new_value", "action", "reason"]
                 ).to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "data_issues.csv", index=False)

    summary = pd.DataFrame(issues).groupby(["column", "action"]).size()
    print(f"Wrote {CLEAN_DIR}/ and {OUTPUT_DIR / 'data_issues.csv'} "
          f"({len(issues)} entries)\n{summary.to_string()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        elif test in TARGET_UNITS and unit != TARGET_UNITS[test]:
            raise SystemExit(f"{name} line {i + 2} (mrn {mrn}): no conversion "
                             f"defined for {test} in {unit!r}")
    return labs


def main():
    CLEAN_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    labs = pd.read_csv(EXPORT_DIR / "lab_results.csv", dtype=str,
                       keep_default_na=False)
    clean_labs(labs).to_csv(CLEAN_DIR / "lab_results.csv", index=False)

    for name in UNCHANGED_FILES:
        shutil.copyfile(EXPORT_DIR / name, CLEAN_DIR / name)

    pd.DataFrame(issues, columns=["file", "line", "mrn", "column", "old_value",

                 ).to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "data_issues.csv", index=False)

    print(f"Wrote {CLEAN_DIR}/ and {OUTPUT_DIR / 'data_issues.csv'} "
          f"({len(issues)} entries)\n{summary.to_string()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
I wrote [clean.py](clean.py) and ran it on the real data. `output/` is now in `.gitignore`, `export/` is untouched (git shows no changes there), and nothing is committed yet.

The run logged 678 entries to `output/data_issues.csv`, one per changed or flagged cell:

| Change | Count |
|---|---|
| Lab dates rewritten as `YYYY-MM-DD` | 425 |
| Test names renamed to a single name | 160 |
| Values converted to a new unit (the unit and reference range were converted with them) | 27 |
| Rows flagged for missing unit | 12 |

- **Dates:** only `DD/MM/YYYY` and `D Mon YY` are accepted. I tested this with a copy of the export where one date was changed to `2025-11-17`; the script stopped with an error naming the line and patient, and exited with an error code.
- **HbA1c:** `A1C` and `Glycated Hb` are now `HbA1c`. The 17 `Glycated Hb` values in mmol/mol were converted to % with the standard formula (% = 0.09148 × mmol/mol + 2.152). For example, 52 became 6.9%.
- **Glucose:** `FBS` and `Glucose (F)` are now `Fasting Glucose`; `PPBS` and `Glucose (PP)` are now `Post Prandial Glucose`. Values in mmol/L were multiplied by 18.016 to get mg/dL, so 5.4 became 97. These new test names were my choice, so tell me if you want different ones.
- **Missing units:** these 12 rows got a `missing_unit` flag and were renamed only, never converted. Three of them are HbA1c rows with values of 65 to 68, which look like mmol/mol, but I left them as they are.

Choices you didn't ask for:

- **Original columns kept:** every lab row keeps its original values in `raw_*` columns next to the cleaned ones.
- **Reference ranges converted:** I converted these along with the values, so 20-42 mmol/mol became 4.0-6.0 %.
- **Unknown units stop the run:** if a renamed test ever arrives in a unit with no defined conversion, the script stops with an error instead of passing it through.
- **Other files copied as-is:** patients, visits and prescriptions are copied to `output/clean/` unchanged. Drug-name cleanup isn't in this step.

"""Hand-written list of diabetes drugs seen in prescriptions.csv.

Matching is exact on a normalised name (dosage-form prefix stripped,
lowercased), never by substring: "Adapalene gel" contains "dapa" but is an
acne gel, not Dapagliflozin.

Usage: python drugs.py [prescriptions.csv]   # prints how each drug name is classified
"""
import re
import sys

import pandas as pd

# Generic names (after normalise()) that are diabetes medications.
DIABETES_DRUGS = {
    # Biguanide
    "metformin",
    "metformin sr",
    # Sulfonylureas
    "glimepiride",
    "glimepiride + metformin",
    "gliclazide mr",
    # DPP-4 inhibitors
    "sitagliptin",
    "vildagliptin",
    # SGLT2 inhibitor (also used for heart failure / CKD without diabetes)
    "dapagliflozin",
    # Alpha-glucosidase inhibitor
    "voglibose",
    # Insulins
    "human mixtard 30/70",
    "insulin aspart",
    "insulin glargine",
    "insulin degludec",
    "insulin lispro",
}

# Checked by hand and deliberately not diabetes drugs.
NOT_DIABETES_DRUGS = {
    "adapalene gel",  # topical retinoid for acne
}

PREFIX = re.compile(r"^(t\.|tab\.?|inj\.|syp)\s+", re.IGNORECASE)


def normalise(drug):
    """'Tab. Metformin SR' / 'T. Metformin SR' / 'TAB METFORMIN SR' -> 'metformin sr'."""
    return PREFIX.sub("", drug.strip()).lower()


def is_diabetes_drug(drug):
    return normalise(drug) in DIABETES_DRUGS


if __name__ == "__main__":
    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "export/prescriptions.csv"
    drugs = pd.read_csv(path, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)["drug"]
    for drug, count in drugs.value_counts().sort_index().items():
        mark = "DIABETES" if is_diabetes_drug(drug) else "-"
        print(f"{mark:9} {drug!r} x{count}")

I made both commits, and the working tree is clean:

- **`648edc4` `feat: clean.py with logged fixes`**: `clean.py` plus the `output/` line in `.gitignore`.
- **`529ef9c` `feat: add hand-written diabetes drug list`**: [drugs.py](drugs.py).

`drugs.py` lists 14 diabetes drugs by hand: metformin (plain and SR), glimepiride (alone and with metformin), gliclazide MR, sitagliptin, vildagliptin, dapagliflozin, voglibose, Human Mixtard 30/70, and insulin aspart, glargine, degludec and lispro.

- **Matching:** before comparing, it strips prefixes like `T.`, `Tab.`, `TAB`, `Inj.` and `Syp`, then lowercases. A name only counts if it matches an entry on the list exactly, never by partial match. That is what keeps Adapalene out: "Adapalene gel" contains "dapa", so a partial match on dapagliflozin would have wrongly caught it.
- **Result:** running `python drugs.py` against the prescriptions marks 33 of the 104 spellings as diabetes drugs. Both Human Mixtard spellings are in, and Adapalene isn't.

Decision for you: dapagliflozin is also prescribed for heart failure and kidney disease in people without diabetes, so a patient on it alone might not be diabetic. I've kept it on the list with a comment saying so. Whether dapagliflozin alone should count toward "diabetic" is part of the definition you'll choose.

# NOTES

## Metformin / insulin are not proof of diabetes
Some diabetes drugs in `export/prescriptions.csv` are given for other reasons (found in `export/visits.csv` notes, all OBG / Dr. Kavya Menon):

- **PCOS on metformin:** SVH025191, SVH029693, SVH030554. Metformin for PCOS, not diabetes.
- **GDM (gestational diabetes):** SVH027966 (metformin), SVH028326 (insulin), SVH028068 (diet only). Pregnancy-only diabetes; may resolve after delivery.
- Related, no drug: SVH028864 "IGT" and SVH024742 "Prediabetes - HbA1c 6.2".

A drug-only rule for "diabetic" would wrongly include the PCOS patients and would count GDM patients as diabetic. Whether GDM / prediabetes count is still an open question for the hospital (see PLAN.md).

## Dapagliflozin
Dapagliflozin is in `drugs.py` but is also prescribed for heart failure and CKD in people without diabetes. A patient on dapagliflozin alone may not be diabetic; check notes / HbA1c before counting them.
EOF
git add NOTES.md && git commit -qm "docs: add NOTES.md on PCOS/GDM metformin and dapagliflozin" && git log --oneline -1 && git push -u origin master 2>&1 | tail -3

I added `NOTES.md`, committed it, and pushed `master`. GitHub already had your push up to `12a8b03`; this push added the three commits after it, ending at `1e2a73a`. You can review `clean.py` here: https://github.com/ManthanNimodiya/Mera-Health-x-Polaris/blob/master/clean.py

I hadn't written up a PCOS/GDM finding before, so I searched the visit notes for it. `NOTES.md` now records what I found:

- **PCOS on metformin:** SVH025191, SVH029693 and SVH030554 take metformin for polycystic ovary syndrome, not diabetes.
- **Gestational diabetes (diabetes in pregnancy):** SVH027966 is on metformin, SVH028326 on insulin, and SVH028068 is on diet control only.
- **Related, with no diabetes drug:** SVH028864 has "IGT" (impaired glucose tolerance) and SVH024742 has "Prediabetes - HbA1c 6.2" in their notes.
- **Dapagliflozin:** it's also prescribed for heart failure and kidney disease, so a patient on it alone may not be diabetic.

All the PCOS and pregnancy cases are OBG visits with Dr. Kavya Menon. If "diabetic" meant "on a diabetes drug", the three PCOS patients would be wrongly included, and so would the two pregnancy-diabetes patients on metformin or insulin. Whether pregnancy diabetes and prediabetes count is still your call.

input.content:
"""List every piece of diabetes evidence per patient, with its source.

Does NOT decide who is diabetic. It only collects evidence:
  drug          - a diabetes drug from drugs.py was prescribed
  note          - a visit note mentions diabetes about the patient
  hba1c_ge_6_5  - a lab HbA1c (in %, after clean.py) is >= 6.5
  diabetology   - the patient had a Diabetology visit
Note mentions that are NOT about the patient having diabetes are kept as
separate context types (never counted as evidence):
  note_negated     - "non-diabetic", "no h/o diabetes", "denies diabetes"
  note_family      - "family history of diabetes", "father diabetic"
  note_gdm         - gestational diabetes / GDM
  note_prediabetes - prediabetes / pre-diabetic / IGT
  hba1c_no_unit    - HbA1c row with no unit (value not interpreted)

Reads output/clean/ (run clean.py first). Writes:
  output/diabetes_evidence.csv             one row per piece of evidence
  output/diabetes_evidence_by_patient.csv  one row per patient
and prints counts per combination of evidence types.

Usage: python evidence.py [output_dir]
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from drugs import is_diabetes_drug

OUTPUT_DIR = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "output")
CLEAN_DIR = OUTPUT_DIR / "clean"
EVIDENCE = ["drug", "note", "hba1c_ge_6_5", "diabetology"]
CONTEXT = ["note_negated", "note_family", "note_gdm", "note_prediabetes",
           "hba1c_no_unit"]

TERM = re.compile(
    r"\b(pre-?diabet\w*|diabet\w*|t[12]dm|dm2|dm|niddm|iddm|gdm|igt)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE)
FAMILY = re.compile(r"\b(family|f/h|father|mother|parents?|brother|sister)\b",
                    re.IGNORECASE)
NEGATION = re.compile(r"\b(non|no|not|denies|nil)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
CLAUSE_BREAK = re.compile(r"[;.]")


def read(name):
    return pd.read_csv(CLEAN_DIR / name, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)


def classify(notes, match):
    """Classify one diabetes term in a note by the clause text before it."""
    term = match.group(1).lower()
    before = CLAUSE_BREAK.split(notes[:match.start()])[-1]
    if term.startswith("pre") or term == "igt":
        return "note_prediabetes"
    if term == "gdm" or "gestational" in before.lower():
        return "note_gdm"
    if FAMILY.search(before):
        return "note_family"
    if NEGATION.search(before):
        return "note_negated"
    return "note"


def collect():
    rows = []

    def add(mrn, kind, source, source_id, date, detail):
        rows.append({"mrn": mrn, "type": kind, "source": source,
                     "source_id": source_id, "date": date, "detail": detail})

    for _, p in read("prescriptions.csv").iterrows():
        if is_diabetes_drug(p["drug"]):
            add(p["mrn"], "drug", "prescriptions.csv", p["visit_id"],
                p["prescribed_on"], f"{p['drug']} {p['dose']}")

    for _, v in read("visits.csv").iterrows():
        if v["department"] == "Diabetology":
            add(v["mrn"], "diabetology", "visits.csv", v["visit_id"],
                v["visit_date"], v["doctor"])
        seen = set()
        for m in TERM.finditer(v["notes"]):
            kind = classify(v["notes"], m)
            if kind not in seen:
                seen.add(kind)
                add(v["mrn"], kind, "visits.csv", v["visit_id"],
                    v["visit_date"], v["notes"])

    labs = read("lab_results.csv")
    for i, lab in labs[labs["test_name"] == "HbA1c"].iterrows():
        source_id = f"line {i + 2}"
        if lab["unit"] == "":
            add(lab["mrn"], "hba1c_no_unit", "lab_results.csv", source_id,
                lab["collected_on"], f"HbA1c {lab['value']} (no unit)")
        elif lab["unit"] != "%":
            raise SystemExit(f"Unexpected HbA1c unit {lab['unit']!r} at {source_id}")
        elif float(lab["value"]) >= 6.5:
            add(lab["mrn"], "hba1c_ge_6_5", "lab_results.csv", source_id,
                lab["collected_on"], f"HbA1c {lab['value']} %")

    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["mrn", "type", "source", "source_id",
                                       "date", "detail"])


def main():
    evidence = collect().sort_values(["mrn", "type", "date"])
    patients = read("patients.csv")[["mrn", "name"]]

    unknown = sorted(set(evidence["mrn"]) - set(patients["mrn"]))
    if unknown:
        print(f"WARNING: evidence for MRNs not in patients.csv: {unknown}")

    counts = evidence.pivot_table(index="mrn", columns="type", values="source",
                                  aggfunc="count", fill_value=0)
    counts = counts.reindex(columns=EVIDENCE + CONTEXT, fill_value=0)
    by_patient = patients.merge(counts, left_on="mrn", right_index=True,
                                how="left").fillna(0)
    by_patient[EVIDENCE + CONTEXT] = by_patient[EVIDENCE + CONTEXT].astype(int)
    by_patient["evidence"] = by_patient[EVIDENCE].apply(
        lambda r: " + ".join(t for t in EVIDENCE if r[t]) or "none", axis=1)
    by_patient["context"] = by_patient[CONTEXT].apply(
        lambda r: " + ".join(t for t in CONTEXT if r[t]), axis=1)

    evidence.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "diabetes_evidence.csv", index=False)
    by_patient.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "diabetes_evidence_by_patient.csv", index=False)

    print(f"{len(evidence)} evidence rows for {evidence['mrn'].nunique()} patients\n")
    print("Patients per evidence combination:")
    print(by_patient["evidence"].value_counts().to_string())
    print("\nPatients with context-only note/lab findings, by evidence combination:")
    with_context = by_patient[by_patient["context"] != ""]
    print(with_context.groupby(["context", "evidence"]).size().to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    print(f"{len(evidence)} evidence rows for {evidence['mrn'].nunique()} patients\n")
    print("Patients per evidence combination:")
    print(by_patient["evidence"].value_counts().to_string())
    print("\nPatients with context-only note/lab findings, by evidence combination:")
    with_context = by_patient[by_patient["context"] != ""]
    print(with_context.groupby(["context", "evidence"]).size().to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
I wrote [evidence.py](evidence.py) and ran it on the cleaned data. It lists every piece of diabetes evidence for each patient with where it came from, and decides nothing. I haven't committed it yet.

It writes two files:
- **`output/diabetes_evidence.csv`**: one row per piece of evidence, with the patient, type, source file, visit ID or line, date and the drug, note or lab value.
- **`output/diabetes_evidence_by_patient.csv`**: one row per patient, with counts of each evidence type.

It looks for four kinds of evidence:
- **Drug:** a diabetes drug from `drugs.py` was prescribed.
- **Note:** a visit note says the patient has diabetes (wording like "T2DM", "DM2", "known diabetic", "k/c/o DM", "NIDDM").
- **HbA1c ≥ 6.5:** a lab HbA1c in %, after `clean.py` has converted units.
- **Diabetology visit.**

Mentions that aren't about the patient having diabetes are kept apart and never counted as evidence. All of them, plus the 165 note matches that did count, looked correct when I checked them by hand:
- **Negated, 4 patients:** "Non-diabetic", "No h/o diabetes", "Denies diabetes".
- **Family history, 4 patients:** "Mother diabetic", "F/h: father diabetic", "family history of diabetes".
- **Pregnancy diabetes, 3 patients.**
- **Prediabetes or IGT, 3 patients.**
- **HbA1c with no unit, 3 patients.**

Patients per combination of evidence:

| Evidence | Patients |
|---|---|
| drug + note + HbA1c + Diabetology | 42 |
| drug + note + HbA1c | 27 |
| drug + note + Diabetology | 11 |
| HbA1c only | 9 |
| drug only | 6 |
| drug + note | 5 |
| drug + HbA1c | 1 |
| drug + HbA1c + Diabetology | 1 |
| none | 198 |

Things in the results to be aware of before you choose a definition:

- **A fourth PCOS patient:** SVH028876's notes say "PCOD" (another name for PCOS), with metformin and an HbA1c of 5.4. They aren't in `NOTES.md` yet. All four PCOS patients have the drug as their only evidence.
- **Drug-only patients:** of the 6, four are PCOS, one is a pregnancy-diabetes patient on insulin (SVH028326), and one is SVH029107, "Shivakumar H M".
- **Evidence split across duplicate records:** SVH029107 looks like the same person as SVH027925 "Shivakumar". Likewise "Md. Rafiq" and "Mohammed Rafiq" (SVH025473 and SVH029873) each have only an HbA1c result. For these two people, part of the evidence sits on each record, so the duplicates need resolving too.
- **Type 1 counts as a note:** the "note" evidence includes Type 1 and juvenile diabetes in Paediatrics, so it isn't Type 2 only.
- **HbA1c written in notes:** some notes contain HbA1c values (for example "HbA1c 6.5"). Only lab HbA1c results are used, not values written in notes.

"""Flag patients that may be the same person, and phones shared by families.

Flags only; never merges or drops anything.

A pair is a possible duplicate only if ALL of these hold:
  - same dob
  - same phone (non-empty)
  - similar name (token rule below)
Same name with a different dob or phone is treated as a different person.

Token rule for "similar name": lowercase, remove dots and apostrophes, split
into words. Similar if every word of the shorter name matches a different
word of the longer name, where two words match if they are equal, one is a
prefix of the other (padma / padmavathi), or they are a hand-listed
abbreviation (md = mohammed).

Reads output/clean/patients.csv. Writes output/possible_duplicates.csv and
output/shared_phones.csv.

Usage: python duplicates.py [output_dir]
"""
import re
import sys
from itertools import combinations
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

OUTPUT_DIR = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "output")
ABBREVIATIONS = {"md": "mohammed"}


def words(name):
    cleaned = re.sub(r"[.']", "", name.lower())
    return [ABBREVIATIONS.get(w, w) for w in cleaned.split()]


def words_match(a, b):
    return a.startswith(b) or b.startswith(a)


def similar_names(name_a, name_b):
    short, long = sorted([words(name_a), words(name_b)], key=len)
    remaining = list(long)
    for w in short:
        match = next((r for r in remaining if words_match(w, r)), None)
        if match is None:
            return False
        remaining.remove(match)
    return True


def main():
    patients = pd.read_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "clean" / "patients.csv", dtype=str,
                           keep_default_na=False)
    with_phone = patients[patients["phone"] != ""]

    pairs = []
    for (dob, phone), group in with_phone.groupby(["dob", "phone"]):
        for (_, a), (_, b) in combinations(group.iterrows(), 2):
            if similar_names(a["name"], b["name"]):
                pairs.append({
                    "mrn_a": a["mrn"], "mrn_b": b["mrn"],
                    "names": f"{a['name']} | {b['name']}",
                    "dob": dob, "phone": phone,
                    "reason": "same dob, same phone, similar name (token rule)",
                })
            else:
                print(f"NOTE: same dob+phone but names not similar, not flagged: "
                      f"{a['mrn']} {a['name']!r} / {b['mrn']} {b['name']!r}")
    duplicates = pd.DataFrame(pairs, columns=["mrn_a", "mrn_b", "names", "dob",
                                              "phone", "reason"])

    # A phone is "shared" if it still covers more than one person after
    # treating each possible-duplicate pair as one person.
    same_person = {row["mrn_b"]: row["mrn_a"] for _, row in duplicates.iterrows()}
    people = with_phone.assign(person=with_phone["mrn"].map(
        lambda m: same_person.get(m, m)))
    people_per_phone = people.groupby("phone")["person"].nunique()
    shared_phones = people_per_phone[people_per_phone > 1].index
    shared = (people[people["phone"].isin(shared_phones)]
              .assign(people_on_phone=lambda d: d["phone"].map(people_per_phone))
              [["phone", "people_on_phone", "mrn", "name", "dob", "sex"]]
              .sort_values(["phone", "dob"]))

    duplicates.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "possible_duplicates.csv", index=False)
    shared.to_csv(OUTPUT_DIR / "shared_phones.csv", index=False)

    print(f"\nPossible duplicates ({len(duplicates)} pairs) -> "
          f"{OUTPUT_DIR / 'possible_duplicates.csv'}")
    print(duplicates.to_string(index=False))
    print(f"\nShared phones, not duplicate pairs ({len(shared_phones)} phones) -> "
          f"{OUTPUT_DIR / 'shared_phones.csv'}")
    print(shared.to_string(index=False))
    print(f"\n({(patients['phone'] == '').sum()} patients have no phone and were "
          f"not compared.)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Work out each patient's follow-up due date and whether they are overdue.

Rules (as chosen; values are passed in, never defaulted here):
  due date = next_appointment on the person's last visit
             else an interval parsed from the last visit's note ("review 6 wks",
             "r/v 3/12", "review tomorrow", "rpt yearly", ...)
             else last visit date + DEFAULT days
  overdue  = due date + GRACE days < AS_OF
             and no visit (by any MRN in a linked duplicate pair) after the due date

A "person" is one MRN, or both MRNs of a pair in output/possible_duplicates.csv.
Only visits on or before AS_OF are used. The rule that set the due date is
recorded. Notes saying the patient died or transferred care are flagged in
`status_flag`; nobody is dropped. This does not filter to diabetic patients.

Reads output/clean/visits.csv, output/clean/patients.csv,
output/possible_duplicates.csv. Writes output/overdue.csv (one row per person
with at least one visit).

Usage: python overdue.py --as-of YYYY-MM-DD --grace-days N --default-days N [--output-dir output]
"""
import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

UNIT = r"(day|days|d|wk|wks|week|weeks|month|months|mth|mths|yr|yrs|year|years)"
INTERVAL_PATTERNS = [
    # "review 6 wks", "Review after 3 months", "rpt after 1 wk",
    # "Rpt HbA1c 6 months", "Rpt TSH 6 wks", "r/v 3 days if fever persists"
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\b(?:\s+[a-z0-9/]+?)??\s+(?:after\s+|in\s+)?"
               rf"(\d+)\s*{UNIT}\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    # "r/v 3/12" = 3 months, "r/v 2/52" = 2 weeks, "r/v 5/7" = 5 days
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\s+(\d+)/(12|52|7)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\s+(tomorrow|yearly)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
]
STATUS_PATTERNS = {
    "deceased": re.compile(r"\bexpired\b|could not be revived|death summary",
                           re.IGNORECASE),
    "transferred": re.compile(r"relocat|transfer(?:red)? (?:of )?care|"
                              r"transfer summary", re.IGNORECASE),
}


def parse_interval(note):
    """Return (pd.DateOffset, matched text) for the first interval found, else None."""
    found = []
    for pattern in INTERVAL_PATTERNS:
        for m in pattern.finditer(note):
            found.append(m)
    if not found:
        return None
    m = min(found, key=lambda m: m.start())
    groups = [g.lower() for g in m.groups()]
    if groups[0] == "tomorrow":
        return pd.DateOffset(days=1), m.group(0)
    if groups[0] == "yearly":
        return pd.DateOffset(years=1), m.group(0)
    n = int(groups[0])
    unit = groups[1]
    if unit in ("12",) or unit.startswith("m"):
        return pd.DateOffset(months=n), m.group(0)
    if unit in ("52",) or unit.startswith("w"):
        return pd.DateOffset(weeks=n), m.group(0)
    if unit in ("7",) or unit.startswith("d"):
        return pd.DateOffset(days=n), m.group(0)
    return pd.DateOffset(years=n), m.group(0)


def to_date(value, where):
    try:
        return pd.Timestamp(pd.to_datetime(value, format="%Y-%m-%d"))
    except ValueError:
        raise SystemExit(f"Bad date {value!r} in {where}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--as-of", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--grace-days", required=True, type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--default-days", required=True, type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", default="output")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    out = Path(args.output_dir)
    as_of = to_date(args.as_of, "--as-of")
    grace = pd.Timedelta(days=args.grace_days)
    default = pd.Timedelta(days=args.default_days)

    read = lambda p: pd.read_csv(p, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    visits = read(out / "clean" / "visits.csv")
    patients = read(out / "clean" / "patients.csv")
    pairs = read(out / "possible_duplicates.csv")

    person_of = {row["mrn_b"]: row["mrn_a"] for _, row in pairs.iterrows()}
    visits["person"] = visits["mrn"].map(lambda m: person_of.get(m, m))
    visits["date"] = [to_date(d, f"visits {v}")
                      for d, v in zip(visits["visit_date"], visits["visit_id"])]
    visits = visits[visits["date"] <= as_of]

    mrns_of = visits.groupby("person")["mrn"].agg(lambda s: " + ".join(sorted(set(s))))
    names = patients.set_index("mrn")[["name", "phone"]]

    rows = []
    for person, pv in visits.sort_values(["date", "visit_id"]).groupby("person"):
        last = pv.iloc[-1]
        if last["next_appointment"]:
            due = to_date(last["next_appointment"], f"visits {last['visit_id']}")
            rule, detail = "next_appointment", last["next_appointment"]
        elif (parsed := parse_interval(last["notes"])) is not None:
            offset, detail = parsed
            due = last["date"] + offset
            rule = "note_interval"
        else:
            due = last["date"] + default
            rule, detail = "default", f"{args.default_days} days"

        after_due = pv[pv["date"] > due]
        statuses = sorted({s for note in pv["notes"]
                           for s, pat in STATUS_PATTERNS.items() if pat.search(note)})
        rows.append({
            "mrns": mrns_of[person],
            "name": names.at[person, "name"] if person in names.index else "",
            "phone": names.at[person, "phone"] if person in names.index else "",
            "last_visit_id": last["visit_id"],
            "last_visit_date": last["visit_date"],
            "last_visit_department": last["department"],
            "due_date": due.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
            "due_rule": rule,
            "due_detail": detail,
            "visits_after_due": len(after_due),
            "days_past_due": (as_of - due).days,
            "overdue": bool(due + grace < as_of and after_due.empty),
            "status_flag": " + ".join(statuses),
        })

    result = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    result.to_csv(out / "overdue.csv", index=False)

    print(f"AS_OF={args.as_of} GRACE={args.grace_days}d DEFAULT={args.default_days}d")
    print(f"{len(result)} people with visits -> {out / 'overdue.csv'}")
    print(result.groupby(["due_rule", "overdue"]).size().to_string())
    flagged = result[result["status_flag"] != ""]
    print(f"\nStatus flags from notes ({len(flagged)}):")
    print(flagged[["mrns", "name", "status_flag", "overdue"]].to_string(index=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

]

    found = []

    groups = [g.lower() for g in m.groups()]

    if unit in ("7",) or unit.startswith("d"):

```bash

```

**How it works:**
- **Linked records count as one person:** both MRNs of a pair from `possible_duplicates.csv` are treated together, and the last visit is taken across both.
- **Due date:** the last visit's `next_appointment` if it has one. Otherwise an interval read from that visit's note, such as "review 6 wks", "Review after 3 months", "r/v 3/12" (3 months), "review tomorrow", "rpt yearly" or "rpt after 1 wk". Otherwise DEFAULT.

Notes with no time interval fall back to DEFAULT, such as "review SOS" (come back if needed), "review with reports" and "rpt FBS/PPBS next visit".
- **Overdue:** due date + GRACE is before AS_OF, and no visit by either linked MRN falls after the due date.
- **Who is included:** visits after AS_OF are ignored. Every patient with a visit gets a row, 296 in all; it doesn't filter to diabetic patients yet.

With the test values, 196 of 296 people come out overdue: 99 set by the default, 50 by `next_appointment` and 47 by a note interval.

1. **Deaths and transfers:** the notes say three patients died: SVH025339, SVH025698 and SVH026086. They also say three transferred their care elsewhere: SVH024860, SVH025512 and SVH028346. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care Section 2 is titled "Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes" and appears in *Diabetes Care* volume 49, supplement 1 (pages S27–S49), published January 2026. Recommendation 2.1a says to diagnose diabetes based on A1C or plasma glucose criteria. The plasma glucose criteria are listed in Table 2.1 and include fasting glucose, 2-hour glucose during a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test, and random glucose with classic hyperglycemic symptoms or crisis.

The search snippets did not show the specific 6.5% A1C cutoff, so I couldn't confirm that threshold from these results. Check Table 2.1 in the full Section 2 text.

Other relevant points:
- The section notes that FPG, 2-h PG during 75-g OGTT, and A1C are appropriate for screening and diagnosis.
- A comparison table covers how these tests differ. A1C is nonfasting and has low within-person variability, but it can be affected by anemia, hemoglobin variants, kidney failure, and other red blood cell conditions.
- The 2026 revisions split Recommendation 2.8 into two parts to stress prompt evaluation of stage 3 (overt) type 1 diabetes in people with islet autoantibodies. Recommendation 2.8b maintains the original guidance that people with multiple islet autoantibodies should be referred to a specialized center.
- The 2024 revisions had already changed the section title and added Recommendation 2.1a to emphasize the structured approach to diagnostic testing.

Sources: the full Section 2 at diabetesjournals.org (doi 10.2337/dc26-S002), the 2026 Summary of Revisions, and the 2026 Abridged Standards of Care for primary care.

"""Impact analysis only: last-visit vs last-diabetes-visit due dates. Changes nothing."""
import re
import sys

import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from drugs import is_diabetes_drug
from evidence import TERM, classify
from overdue import INTERVAL_PATTERNS, STATUS_PATTERNS

AS_OF = pd.Timestamp("2026-09-29")
GRACE = pd.Timedelta(days=14)
DIAB_WORDS = re.compile(r"\b(hba1c|sugars?|fbs|ppbs)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
LAB_RPT = re.compile(r"^rpt\s+(?!after\b|\d)(\S+)", re.IGNORECASE)

r = lambda p: pd.read_csv(p, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
b = r("output/diabetes_evidence_by_patient.csv")
for c in ["drug", "note", "hba1c_ge_6_5", "diabetology"]:
    b[c] = b[c].astype(int) > 0
rule = b[b.drug & (b.note | b.hba1c_ge_6_5 | b.diabetology)]
pairs = r("output/possible_duplicates.csv")
person_of = dict(zip(pairs.mrn_b, pairs.mrn_a))
visits = r("output/clean/visits.csv")
visits["person"] = visits.mrn.map(lambda m: person_of.get(m, m))
dead = {person_of.get(m, m) for m, n in zip(visits.mrn, visits.notes)
        if any(p.search(n) for p in STATUS_PATTERNS.values())}
people = set(rule.mrn.map(lambda m: person_of.get(m, m))) - {"SVH027966"} - dead
assert len(people) == 79, len(people)

rx = r("output/clean/prescriptions.csv")
drug_visits = set(rx[rx.drug.map(is_diabetes_drug)].visit_id)


def mentions_diabetes(note):
    if DIAB_WORDS.search(note):
        return True
    return any(classify(note, m) == "note" for m in TERM.finditer(note))


visits["date"] = pd.to_datetime(visits.visit_date, format="%Y-%m-%d")
visits = visits[(visits.date <= AS_OF) & visits.person.isin(people)]
visits["diab"] = ((visits.department == "Diabetology")
                  | visits.notes.map(mentions_diabetes)
                  | visits.visit_id.isin(drug_visits))


def interval(note):
    found = sorted((m for p in INTERVAL_PATTERNS for m in p.finditer(note)),
                   key=lambda m: m.start())
    for m in found:
        lab = LAB_RPT.match(m.group(0))
        if lab and lab.group(1).lower() not in ("hba1c", "fbs", "ppbs", "fbs/ppbs"):
            continue  # non-diabetes lab repeat, e.g. "rpt TSH 6 wks"
        g = [x.lower() for x in m.groups()]
        if g[0] == "tomorrow":
            return pd.DateOffset(days=1), m.group(0)
        if g[0] == "yearly":
            return pd.DateOffset(years=1), m.group(0)
        n, u = int(g[0]), g[1]
        if u == "12" or u.startswith("m"):
            return pd.DateOffset(months=n), m.group(0)
        if u == "52" or u.startswith("w"):
            return pd.DateOffset(weeks=n), m.group(0)
        if u == "7" or u.startswith("d"):
            return pd.DateOffset(days=n), m.group(0)
        return pd.DateOffset(years=n), m.group(0)
    return None


def due_from(v, default_months):
    if v.next_appointment:
        return pd.Timestamp(v.next_appointment), "next_appointment"
    if (iv := interval(v.notes)) is not None:
        return v.date + iv[0], f"note: {iv[1]}"
    return v.date + pd.DateOffset(months=default_months), "default"


def evaluate(default_months):
    rows = []
    for person, pv in visits.sort_values(["date", "visit_id"]).groupby("person"):
        last_any = pv.iloc[-1]
        dv = pv[pv.diab]
        last_d = dv.iloc[-1]
        due_cur, _ = due_from(last_any, default_months)
        due, why = due_from(last_d, default_months)
        after_any = pv[pv.date > due]
        after_diab = after_any[after_any.diab]
        late = due + GRACE < AS_OF
        rows.append(dict(
            person=person, mrns=" + ".join(sorted(set(pv.mrn))),
            last_visit=f"{last_any.visit_date} {last_any.department}",
            last_is_diab=bool(last_any.diab),
            last_diab_visit=f"{last_d.visit_date} {last_d.department} ({last_d.visit_id})",
            due=due.date(), due_rule=why,
            current=bool(due_cur + GRACE < AS_OF and pv[pv.date > due_cur].empty),
            A=bool(late and after_any.empty), B=bool(late and after_diab.empty),
            later_visits="; ".join(f"{x.visit_date} {x.department}{' [diab]' if x.diab else ''}"
                                   for x in pv[pv.date > last_d.date].itertuples()),
        ))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


res = evaluate(3)
print(f"People: {len(res)}")
print(f"1. Last visit NOT diabetes-related: {(~res.last_is_diab).sum()}")
print(res[~res.last_is_diab][["mrns", "last_visit", "last_diab_visit"]].to_string(index=False))
print("\n2. Overdue (DEFAULT 3 months, GRACE 14d, AS_OF 2026-09-29):")
print(f"   current overdue.py rule (last visit of any kind): {res.current.sum()}")
print(f"   A: {res.A.sum()}   B: {res.B.sum()}")
print("   due rule used (A/B):", res.due_rule.str.replace(r"note: .*", "note", regex=True).value_counts().to_dict())
flips = res[res.A != res.B]
print(f"\n3. Flips between A and B: {len(flips)}")
for x in flips.itertuples():
    print(f"  {x.mrns}: A={x.A} B={x.B}; last diabetes visit {x.last_diab_visit}, due {x.due} ({x.due_rule})\n"
          f"      later visits: {x.later_visits}")
res6 = evaluate(6)
print(f"\n4. DEFAULT 6 months: current {res6.current.sum()}  A {res6.A.sum()}  B {res6.B.sum()}")
print("   (using DEFAULT for", (res6.due_rule == "default").sum(), "people)")
changed = res.merge(res6, on="person", suffixes=("_3", "_6"))
for opt in "AB":
    ch = changed[changed[f"{opt}_3"] != changed[f"{opt}_6"]]
    print(f"   {opt}: overdue at 3 months but not at 6: {', '.join(ch.mrns_3)}")

I committed DECISIONS.md as `d738c26` `docs: diabetic count chain, died/transferred list, shared phones`. It isn't pushed. `overdue.py` is unchanged: I ran the analysis as a separate script in my scratch folder.

All runs below use AS_OF 2026-09-29, GRACE 14 days and DEFAULT 3 months, with linked duplicate pairs counted as one person. They cover your 79 people.

**Your "diabetes-related" definition misses some diabetes visits.** Three of the last visits it classed as unrelated are clearly diabetes follow-ups:
- **SVH025331:** "Follow up visit. Home GRBS 102-162. Missed meds x 2 wks" (GRBS is a home blood-sugar reading).
- **SVH025948:** "f/u visit; home GRBS 148-215; urine microalbumin adv".
- **SVH026465:** "f/u visit. F 149 / PP 258. Dose stepped up" (fasting and after-meal sugar readings).

I'd add `GRBS`/`RBS` and the `F # / PP #` shorthand. I ran both versions:

| | Your definition as written | + GRBS/RBS and F/PP (recommended) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Last visit not diabetes-related | 9 | 6 |
| 2. Overdue under the current `overdue.py` rule (last visit of any kind) | 36 | 36 |
| Option A (any later visit counts) | 33 | 35 |
| Option B (only a later diabetes visit counts) | 42 | 41 |
| 3. Patients who flip between A and B | 9 | 6 |
| 4. DEFAULT 6 months instead of 3: current / A / B | 34 / 31 / 40 | 34 / 33 / 39 |

For option A, I took "any later visit" to mean any visit after the due date, which is the rule in `overdue.py` now. Changing DEFAULT to 6 months only takes two people off the overdue list, SVH029625 and SVH029767, under both options.

**The 6 who flip, with the wider definition.** All are overdue under B and not under A:

| Person | Last diabetes visit | Due date (rule) | Later visits |
|---|---|---|---|
| SVH026153 | 2025-11-26 General Medicine | 2026-01-07 (note: "Review 6 wks") | 2026-08-14 ENT |
| SVH026193 | 2025-08-27 General Medicine | 2025-11-27 (note: "review 3 months") | 2026-08-04 Dental |
| SVH027082 + SVH030772 (Padma Reddy) | 2025-08-08 Diabetology | 2025-11-08 (default) | 2026-07-27 General Medicine, a thyroid visit ("rpt TSH 6 wks") |
| SVH027261 | 2025-11-23 General Medicine | 2025-12-20 (next_appointment) | 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-16 Dermatology |
| SVH027925 + SVH029107 (Shivakumar) | 2025-06-11 General Medicine | 2025-10-12 (next_appointment) | 2026-08-26 Orthopaedics |
| SVH029007 | 2025-01-14 General Medicine | 2025-02-28 (next_appointment) | 2026-01-17 Ophthalmology; 2026-01-26 General Medicine: "Routine f/u. Dose stepped up. Review after 3 months" |

The first five are exactly your concern: an ENT, Dental, thyroid, skin or orthopaedic visit is hiding a missed diabetes follow-up. Option B catches them and A doesn't.

SVH029007 is borderline. Its last visit says "Dose stepped up", which is likely a diabetes medicine, but no diabetes drug was prescribed at that visit and the note names no sugar reading. If it is a diabetes visit, the due date would come from it ("Review after 3 months" → 2026-04-26), and they'd still be overdue.

My recommendation is option B with the wider definition: 41 overdue at DEFAULT 3 months. Tell me which option and DEFAULT you want, and I'll change `overdue.py`.

"""Work out each patient's diabetes follow-up due date and whether they are overdue.

Rules (see DECISIONS.md):
  diabetes-related visit = Diabetology, OR a diabetes drug prescribed at that
      visit, OR the note mentions diabetes / HbA1c / sugars / FBS / PPBS /
      GRBS / RBS or "F # / PP #" readings
  due date = on the person's LAST diabetes-related visit:
             next_appointment
             else an interval parsed from its note ("review 6 wks", "r/v 3/12",
                  "review tomorrow", "rpt HbA1c 3 months", ...); lab repeats
                  count only for HbA1c/FBS/PPBS ("rpt TSH 6 wks" is ignored)
             else visit date + DEFAULT months
  overdue  = due date + GRACE days < AS_OF
             and no diabetes-related visit (by any MRN in a linked duplicate
             pair) after the due date

A "person" is one MRN, or both MRNs of a pair in output/possible_duplicates.csv.
Only visits on or before AS_OF are used. The rule that set the due date is
recorded. Notes saying the patient died or transferred care are flagged in
`status_flag`; nobody is dropped. People with no diabetes-related visit get no
row. This does not filter to diabetic patients.

Reads output/clean/{visits,patients,prescriptions}.csv and
output/possible_duplicates.csv. Writes output/overdue.csv.

Usage: python overdue.py --as-of YYYY-MM-DD --grace-days N --default-months N [--output-dir output]
"""
import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from drugs import is_diabetes_drug
from evidence import TERM, classify

UNIT = r"(day|days|d|wk|wks|week|weeks|month|months|mth|mths|yr|yrs|year|years)"
INTERVAL_PATTERNS = [
    # "review 6 wks", "Review after 3 months", "rpt after 1 wk",
    # "Rpt HbA1c 6 months", "Rpt TSH 6 wks", "r/v 3 days if fever persists"
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\b(?:\s+[a-z0-9/]+?)??\s+(?:after\s+|in\s+)?"
               rf"(\d+)\s*{UNIT}\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    # "r/v 3/12" = 3 months, "r/v 2/52" = 2 weeks, "r/v 5/7" = 5 days
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\s+(\d+)/(12|52|7)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\s+(tomorrow|yearly)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
]
# "rpt <test> ..." where <test> is not a diabetes test is not a follow-up date.
LAB_REPEAT = re.compile(r"^rpt\s+(?!after\b|\d)(\S+)", re.IGNORECASE)
DIABETES_LAB_TESTS = {"hba1c", "fbs", "ppbs", "fbs/ppbs"}
DIABETES_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"\b(hba1c|sugars?|fbs|ppbs|grbs|rbs)\b|\bF \d+ / PP \d+", re.IGNORECASE)
STATUS_PATTERNS = {
    "deceased": re.compile(r"\bexpired\b|could not be revived|death summary",
                           re.IGNORECASE),
    "transferred": re.compile(r"relocat|transfer(?:red)? (?:of )?care|"
                              r"transfer summary", re.IGNORECASE),
}


def parse_interval(note):
    """Return (pd.DateOffset, matched text) for the first usable interval, else None."""
    found = sorted((m for p in INTERVAL_PATTERNS for m in p.finditer(note)),
                   key=lambda m: m.start())
    for m in found:
        lab = LAB_REPEAT.match(m.group(0))
        if lab and lab.group(1).lower() not in DIABETES_LAB_TESTS:
            continue
        groups = [g.lower() for g in m.groups()]
        if groups[0] == "tomorrow":
            return pd.DateOffset(days=1), m.group(0)
        if groups[0] == "yearly":
            return pd.DateOffset(years=1), m.group(0)
        n, unit = int(groups[0]), groups[1]
        if unit == "12" or unit.startswith("m"):
            return pd.DateOffset(months=n), m.group(0)
        if unit == "52" or unit.startswith("w"):
            return pd.DateOffset(weeks=n), m.group(0)
        if unit == "7" or unit.startswith("d"):
            return pd.DateOffset(days=n), m.group(0)
        return pd.DateOffset(years=n), m.group(0)
    return None


def mentions_diabetes(note):
    if DIABETES_WORDS.search(note):
        return True
    return any(classify(note, m) == "note" for m in TERM.finditer(note))


def to_date(value, where):
    try:
        return pd.Timestamp(pd.to_datetime(value, format="%Y-%m-%d"))
    except ValueError:
        raise SystemExit(f"Bad date {value!r} in {where}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("--as-of", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--grace-days", required=True, type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--default-months", required=True, type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", default="output")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    out = Path(args.output_dir)
    as_of = to_date(args.as_of, "--as-of")
    grace = pd.Timedelta(days=args.grace_days)
    default = pd.DateOffset(months=args.default_months)

    read = lambda p: pd.read_csv(p, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    visits = read(out / "clean" / "visits.csv")
    patients = read(out / "clean" / "patients.csv")
    prescriptions = read(out / "clean" / "prescriptions.csv")
    pairs = read(out / "possible_duplicates.csv")

    person_of = {row["mrn_b"]: row["mrn_a"] for _, row in pairs.iterrows()}
    visits["person"] = visits["mrn"].map(lambda m: person_of.get(m, m))
    visits["date"] = [to_date(d, f"visits {v}")
                      for d, v in zip(visits["visit_date"], visits["visit_id"])]
    visits = visits[visits["date"] <= as_of]
    drug_visits = set(prescriptions.loc[prescriptions["drug"].map(is_diabetes_drug),
                                        "visit_id"])
    visits["diabetes_visit"] = ((visits["department"] == "Diabetology")
                                | visits["visit_id"].isin(drug_visits)
                                | visits["notes"].map(mentions_diabetes))

    mrns_of = visits.groupby("person")["mrn"].agg(lambda s: " + ".join(sorted(set(s))))
    names = patients.set_index("mrn")[["name", "phone"]]

    rows = []
    for person, pv in visits.sort_values(["date", "visit_id"]).groupby("person"):
        diabetes_visits = pv[pv["diabetes_visit"]]
        if diabetes_visits.empty:
            continue
        last = diabetes_visits.iloc[-1]
        if last["next_appointment"]:
            due = to_date(last["next_appointment"], f"visits {last['visit_id']}")
            rule, detail = "next_appointment", last["next_appointment"]
        elif (parsed := parse_interval(last["notes"])) is not None:
            offset, detail = parsed
            due = last["date"] + offset
            rule = "note_interval"
        else:
            due = last["date"] + default
            rule, detail = "default", f"{args.default_months} months"

        after_due = diabetes_visits[diabetes_visits["date"] > due]
        later = pv[pv["date"] > last["date"]]
        statuses = sorted({s for note in pv["notes"]
                           for s, pat in STATUS_PATTERNS.items() if pat.search(note)})
        rows.append({
            "person": person,
            "mrns": mrns_of[person],
            "name": names.at[person, "name"] if person in names.index else "",
            "phone": names.at[person, "phone"] if person in names.index else "",
            "last_diabetes_visit_id": last["visit_id"],
            "last_diabetes_visit_date": last["visit_date"],
            "last_diabetes_visit_department": last["department"],
            "last_diabetes_visit_doctor": last["doctor"],
            "due_date": due.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
            "due_rule": rule,
            "due_detail": detail,
            "diabetes_visits_after_due": len(after_due),
            "later_other_visits": "; ".join(
                f"{v.visit_date} {v.department}"
                for v in later[~later["diabetes_visit"]].itertuples()),
            "days_past_due": (as_of - due).days,
            "overdue": bool(due + grace < as_of and after_due.empty),
            "status_flag": " + ".join(statuses),
        })

    result = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    result.to_csv(out / "overdue.csv", index=False)

    print(f"AS_OF={args.as_of} GRACE={args.grace_days}d DEFAULT={args.default_months} months")
    print(f"{len(result)} people with a diabetes-related visit -> {out / 'overdue.csv'}")
    print(result.groupby(["due_rule", "overdue"]).size().to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Work out each patient's follow-up due date and whether they are overdue.

Rules (as chosen; values are passed in, never defaulted here):
  due date = next_appointment on the person's last visit
             else an interval parsed from the last visit's note ("review 6 wks",
             "r/v 3/12", "review tomorrow", "rpt yearly", ...)
             else last visit date + DEFAULT days
  overdue  = due date + GRACE days < AS_OF
             and no visit (by any MRN in a linked duplicate pair) after the due date

A "person" is one MRN, or both MRNs of a pair in output/possible_duplicates.csv.
Only visits on or before AS_OF are used. The rule that set the due date is
recorded. Notes saying the patient died or transferred care are flagged in
`status_flag`; nobody is dropped. This does not filter to diabetic patients.

Reads output/clean/visits.csv, output/clean/patients.csv,
output/possible_duplicates.csv. Writes output/overdue.csv (one row per person

import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

UNIT = r"(day|days|d|wk|wks|week|weeks|month|months|mth|mths|yr|yrs|year|years)"
INTERVAL_PATTERNS = [
    # "review 6 wks", "Review after 3 months", "rpt after 1 wk",
    # "Rpt HbA1c 6 months", "Rpt TSH 6 wks", "r/v 3 days if fever persists"
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\b(?:\s+[a-z0-9/]+?)??\s+(?:after\s+|in\s+)?"
               rf"(\d+)\s*{UNIT}\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    # "r/v 3/12" = 3 months, "r/v 2/52" = 2 weeks, "r/v 5/7" = 5 days
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\s+(\d+)/(12|52|7)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
    re.compile(r"\b(?:review|r/v|rpt)\s+(tomorrow|yearly)\b", re.IGNORECASE),
]
STATUS_PATTERNS = {
    "deceased": re.compile(r"\bexpired\b|could not be revived|death summary",
                           re.IGNORECASE),
    "transferred": re.compile(r"relocat|transfer(?:red)? (?:of )?care|"
                              r"transfer summary", re.IGNORECASE),
}


def parse_interval(note):
    """Return (pd.DateOffset, matched text) for the first interval found, else None."""
    found = []
    for pattern in INTERVAL_PATTERNS:
        for m in pattern.finditer(note):
            found.append(m)
    if not found:
        return None
    m = min(found, key=lambda m: m.start())
    groups = [g.lower() for g in m.groups()]
    if groups[0] == "tomorrow":
        return pd.DateOffset(days=1), m.group(0)
    if groups[0] == "yearly":
        return pd.DateOffset(years=1), m.group(0)
    n = int(groups[0])
    unit = groups[1]
    if unit in ("12",) or unit.startswith("m"):
        return pd.DateOffset(months=n), m.group(0)
    if unit in ("52",) or unit.startswith("w"):
        return pd.DateOffset(weeks=n), m.group(0)
    if unit in ("7",) or unit.startswith("d"):
        return pd.DateOffset(days=n), m.group(0)
    return pd.DateOffset(years=n), m.group(0)

    try:

    except ValueError:
        raise SystemExit(f"Bad date {value!r} in {where}")

    visits = visits[visits["date"] <= as_of]

    mrns_of = visits.groupby("person")["mrn"].agg(lambda s: " + ".join(sorted(set(s))))
    names = patients.set_index("mrn")[["name", "phone"]]

        if last["next_appointment"]:

            "phone": names.at[person, "phone"] if person in names.index else "",

            "last_visit_date": last["visit_date"],
            "last_visit_department": last["department"],
            "due_date": due.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
            "due_rule": rule,
            "due_detail": detail,
            "visits_after_due": len(after_due),
            "days_past_due": (as_of - due).days,

            "status_flag": " + ".join(statuses),
        })

    result = pd.DataFrame(rows)

    print(f"{len(result)} people with visits -> {out / 'overdue.csv'}")
    print(result.groupby(["due_rule", "overdue"]).size().to_string())

# mera.health Engineering Intern Take-Home

**A hospital sent us this**

## Context

mera.health works directly with hospitals to digitise and organise their patient records. A lot of that work starts the same way: someone at a hospital sends a short email and a data export, and we have to work out what they need.

This is one of those. The hospital and patients are fictional. The email and the mess are realistic.

## What we're giving you

- `email.txt`: a message from the hospital's operations manager.
- `export/`: what they attached. Four CSV files, about 2,000 rows in all: `patients.csv`, `visits.csv`, `lab_results.csv`, `prescriptions.csv`.

The email, in full:

> Hi team,
>
> Our doctors want to see which diabetic patients are overdue for follow-up so the front desk can call them. Export from our system attached. Can you put something together?
>
> Thanks,
> Meenakshi

## What you'll build

Something that answers her request and that the hospital could use. What form that takes is your call. It has to run on our laptop with one or two commands. No login, no deployment.

## What we want to see

The email leaves almost everything undefined, and the export isn't clean. Working out what the request means, and what the data can and can't support, is the task. Building the thing is the easy part.

Alongside the code, we want:

1. **`PLAN.md`**, committed before you or your agent write any code. How you're breaking this down, what you need to find out first, what you're unsure about. Half a page. It's fine if the plan turns out wrong. Don't go back and edit it.
2. **`DECISIONS.md`**, two pages at most:
   - Each term in the email you had to define, the definition you chose, and why.
   - Each problem you found in the data, and what you did about it.
   - Where you chose to flag something for a person to check rather than decide yourself.
   - What your result can't be trusted for.
3. **`reply.txt`**: the email you'd send back to Meenakshi with your result. 200 words at most. She isn't technical and she isn't a doctor.

## You can ask us questions

You may send us one email with up to five questions, as if you were writing to the hospital. We'll reply within one working day. You don't have to wait for the reply to keep working.

What you ask is part of what we look at. So is what you decide not to ask and work out yourself.

## How we expect you to work

We expect you to use an AI coding agent: Claude Code, Cursor, whatever you like. We use them every day. Writing the code is the cheap part now, so the code isn't what we're assessing. We're assessing how you approached the problem: how you broke it down, what you asked the agent to do, where you disagreed with it, and what you checked yourself.

One warning. If you paste the email into an agent and ask it to build something, it will. It will pick a meaning for "diabetic" and a meaning for "overdue" without telling you, and it will produce a confident list. Noticing that is your job.

So please:

- **Send your agent transcripts.** Export your sessions and include them unedited. This is strongly encouraged, not required. If we move to the next step, explaining your approach is part of the evaluation, and the transcript is the best record you'll have of what you did and why. It helps you as much as it helps us.
- **Keep your real git history.** Commit as you go. Don't squash.

A messy transcript where you changed your mind is better than a clean one.

You don't need medical knowledge, and you don't need a paid API. You will need to look a few things up. Tell us what you looked up and where.

## Time

About 4 hours of work. Please don't spend more. If you run out of time, stop and tell us what you'd do next. Send it back within 5 days of receiving it.

## How we'll evaluate you

About half of this is your process and half is what came out of it.

**Process**
1. **Breaking it down.** Did you work out what the question was before answering it?
2. **Working with the agent.** When it guessed, did you notice? What did you check yourself?
3. **Questions.** Did you ask the things that would change what you built?

**Outcome**
4. **Definitions.** Are your meanings for "diabetic" and "overdue" reasoned, and do you know who they wrongly include or leave out?
5. **Care with the data.** This is people's health data. "Roughly right" isn't good enough, and a wrong name on a call list is a real phone call to a real person.
6. **Usefulness.** Could the front desk use what you built on Monday morning? Does your reply tell Meenakshi what she needs to know?

## What to submit

- The code, as a repo link or zip, with its git history and run instructions.
- `PLAN.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `reply.txt`.
- Your agent transcripts, if you're sharing them.

## What we're not looking for

- A beautiful UI. Plain is fine.
- Finding every problem in the data. Nobody will.
- A long list of technologies.
- Tests, CI, Docker, anything you don't need.

## What will get you rejected

- A list of patients with no explanation of how they got on it.
- Data changed, merged or dropped silently, with no mention in `DECISIONS.md`.
- Work you can't explain. "The AI wrote it" isn't an answer.

## After you submit

If we move forward, a 30 minute call. You'll walk us through your approach, we'll ask about specific moments in it, and then Meenakshi will reply with a follow-up request and we'll see how you'd handle it.
Hi team,

Our doctors want to see which diabetic patients are overdue for follow-up so the front desk can call them. Export from our system attached. Can you put something together?

Thanks,
Meenakshi

# DECISIONS

## 1. Terms I had to define

**As-of date.** Passed in (`--as-of 2026-09-29`, the last date in the export); the code never uses today's date. *Why:* the same export always gives the same list.

**Diabetic** = on a diabetes drug AND at least one of: a note saying diabetic, HbA1c >= 6.5 %, a Diabetology visit. Gestational diabetes (GDM, diabetes in pregnancy) and metformin for PCOS do not count. *Why:* a drug alone is not proof (metformin is also used for PCOS, dapagliflozin for heart failure and kidney disease); a lab result alone has no treating doctor behind it. 87 records -> 86 people (one duplicate pair) -> 85 (GDM moved to doctor review) -> 79 (6 died or transferred).
*Wrongly leaves out:* diabetics managed by diet only, diabetics with no drug or note in this export. *Wrongly includes:* anyone whose diabetes note or drug is a data-entry error.

**Diabetes-related visit** = Diabetology, OR a diabetes drug prescribed at that visit, OR the note mentions diabetes / HbA1c / sugars / FBS / PPBS / GRBS / RBS / "F # / PP #". *Why:* a dental, ENT or skin visit doesn't check diabetes. *Misses:* a diabetes visit written without these words (SVH029007, flagged).

**Follow-up / due date** = from the last diabetes-related visit: its next_appointment, else the interval in its note ("review 6 wks", "r/v 3/12"), else 3 months. Lab repeats count only for HbA1c/FBS/PPBS ("rpt TSH 6 wks" is ignored). *Why 3 months:* ADA advises HbA1c every 3 months if not at target, twice a year if stable; I took the cautious end.

**Overdue** = due date + 14 days grace is before the as-of date, AND no later diabetes-related visit (under either record of a duplicate pair). Result: 41. If any later visit counted, it would be 35; with a 6-month default, 39. *Wrongly includes:* someone seen elsewhere, or whose follow-up was only a phone call. *Wrongly leaves out:* someone whose later visit mentioned sugars but didn't really review diabetes.

## 2. Data problems and what I did
Every change is logged row by row in `output/data_issues.csv`; nothing was dropped or merged.

- **Lab dates in 3 formats** (`03/04/2024`, `14 Oct 23`, `2 Oct 23`). For the slash dates, 238 have a first number > 12 and none a second number > 12, so they are DD/MM. All converted to YYYY-MM-DD; any other format stops the script.
- **Two lab dates after the export end** (2026-12-19 and 2027-02-27, SVH027355 and SVH030138). Not fixed. Neither patient's status depends on them.
- **HbA1c under 3 names** (HbA1c, A1C, Glycated Hb); Glycated Hb in mmol/mol converted to %: % = 0.09148 x mmol/mol + 2.152 (NGSP).
- **Glucose under several names** (FBS, Glucose (F), PPBS...) and some in mmol/L; converted to mg/dL (x 18.016).
- **12 lab rows with no unit**, including 3 HbA1c of 65-68 (probably mmol/mol). Flagged, not converted or guessed.
- **Drug name variants** ("Metformin", "T. Metformin", "Tab. Metformin"): prefixes stripped, matched exactly against a hand-written list. Exact match keeps "Adapalene gel" (acne) from matching dapagliflozin; "Human Mixtard" (insulin) is included.
- **Duplicate patients:** 4 pairs with the same date of birth, same phone and a similar name (e.g. "Md. Rafiq" / "Mohammed Rafiq"). Linked for counting and the "visited since?" check, not merged. Padma Reddy's July 2026 visit is under her second record.
- **Shared phones:** 3 numbers with 3 people each. **Missing phones:** 8 patients, 3 on the call list.
- **Died / transferred** is only in visit notes (3 each). Moved to "Not called" with the note quoted.
- **Metformin for PCOS/PCOD** (4) and **GDM** (3) found in notes; excluded from "diabetic".

## 3. Flagged for a person instead of decided
- **Doctor review, do not call yet (16):** HbA1c >= 6.5 with no diabetes drug or note (8), HbA1c with no unit (2), GDM (3), prediabetes/IGT (3).
- **Duplicate pairs:** shown on the list with the other record number; the hospital should merge them.
- **SVH029007:** last visit "Dose stepped up. Review after 3 months" may be a diabetes visit. Overdue either way.
- **HbA1c without units:** on the review list, and flagged on the call list for one patient.
- **Shared phones:** front desk asks for the patient by name before giving the reason.

## 4. What this can't be trusted for
- Deaths or transfers not written in a visit note: such patients would still be called.
- Patients treated at another hospital or clinic.
- Diagnoses never written in notes, prescriptions or labs here.
- Anything after 2026-09-29, when the export ends.
- Notes are searched by keywords; unusual wording or spelling can be missed.
- The 3-month default and 14-day grace are my choices, not the hospital's.
- Questions sent to the hospital, still unanswered: Does prediabetes or diabetes in pregnancy count as diabetic? What follow-up interval applies when the doctor wrote none? Does any later visit count as follow-up, or only a diabetes one?

## What I looked up
- ADA Standards of Care 2026, Section 2 (HbA1c >= 6.5 % for diagnosis): https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926/2-Diagnosis-and-Classification-of-Diabetes
- ADA Standards of Care 2026, Section 6 (HbA1c testing frequency): https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S132/163927
- HbA1c mmol/mol to % conversion (NGSP): https://ngsp.org/ifccngsp.asp
- Glucose mmol/L to mg/dL: x 18.016 (glucose molar mass 180.16 g/mol / 10).
- Medical shorthand: "r/v 3/12" = review in 3 months (/52 weeks, /7 days); "x 2/52" = for 2 weeks (a symptom's duration, not a review date); GRBS = home blood sugar; F/PP = fasting / after-meal sugar; IGT = impaired glucose tolerance.

## Where I disagreed with the agent / what it caught
- **It caught:** my diabetes-visit definition missed GRBS and "F # / PP #" readings, so 3 real diabetes follow-ups looked like non-diabetes visits.
- **It caught:** my first count of 81 didn't match my own rule (87); that led to the 87 -> 86 -> 85 -> 79 chain.
- **It caught:** I called the 3 shared phones "family phones", but one number has 3 women with different surnames, so I changed the wording.
- **I overruled:** it wanted to pick definitions itself (the containment rule for names missed 2 of my 4 duplicate examples; it proposed a word-by-word rule and I chose it).
